bug_semantics: OliveTin's public /oauth/login handler inserts a new per-request OAuth2 state into an in-memory map (registeredStates) and never expires, deletes, or bounds those entries. An unauthenticated client can flood /oauth/login (configured OAuth2 provider required) and grow the map until memory is exhausted; HandleOAuthCallback only updates existing entries, and later logout RevokeSession delete plus the CVE-2026-28789 mutex do not cap growth. Distinct from GHSA-45m3-398w-m2m9 / CVE-2026-28789 (unsynchronized map panic).
flaw_origin: The unbounded-map mechanism was first written in 6a7187fb5b6a7fa900d7df0f0da8fdb3ebf02734 (2024-10-14, 'feature: OAuth2! :-D'): package-level registeredStates = make(map[string]*oauth2State) and handleOAuthLogin assigning registeredStates[state] with no TTL, delete, or max size, while singleFrontend.go registered /oauth/login publicly. Later rename/move/mutex/refactor commits preserved that insert; they are not the BIC.
